text: Forgot to mention - Westbrook emailed yesterday, Anna's science exhibition is Thursday at 4. I have the Huxley lab seminar until 5:30 so you'd need to cover pickup.
Thursday works. Is it the whole grade or just her cohort?
Her cohort, I think. Maybe 20 kids. She's presenting the seed germination project, the one she redid three times because the control group 'didn't look right.'
Ha. She definitely gets that from you. Should I bring Karen or is it parents only?
Parents only, per the email. Karen can hear about it at dinner Saturday. Anna will narrate every detail unprompted, I promise.
Fair. I'll leave the office by 3:30. Good luck with Huxley - try not to eviscerate anyone's methodology this time. 😬
mom my bio teacher wants us to model a protein interaction for our final project and i have NO idea where to start. everyone else is doing the covid spike protein and i really don't want to copy them

Good instinct, spike protein is overexposed. Consider hemoglobin's allosteric transition or an AlphaFold2 prediction target if you want something current. What software does your teacher expect you to use?
she said anything that runs on a school chromebook so nothing too intense 😭 also can you ask Karen what she thinks? she always has the coolest ideas

Karen's specialty is population genetics, not structural biology. Different field entirely. For Chromebook constraints, Mol* Viewer with a pre-loaded PDB file will work fine. I'll pull three good candidate structures tonight.
ok yes please!! also can you bring granola bars when you pick me up? not the fig ones, those are genuinely terrible
I'll check the pantry. Be outside Westbrook at 3:45 - I have a faculty meeting at 4:30 and I'm not circling the lot.

Dad, Anna's Westbrook science fair is Thursday. She built her entire project around protein folding analogies using pipe cleaners. I'll be honest, I spent more of my morning focus block on it than my actual grant revision.
Ha! Is she the only one not doing a baking soda volcano?
One child constructed a 'working' heart from balloons. I'll grant full marks for ambition and deduct accordingly for anything resembling anatomy.
Does Steve know what protein folding is yet or is he just nodding along supportively?
He laminated the display borders. Color-coordinated, perfectly straight, zero scientific content. Which is genuinely the best division of labor we've landed on. Anna's presenting the slides herself.
I expect a photo Thursday. Tell her grandpa wants a full debrief. 🧬
